# 1 Chronicles Chapter 21 — The PNEUMA Bible (Dynamic)
**Translator:** PNEUMA | **Source:** Leningrad Codex (B19A), Folios 381r–381v

---

**1** Satan rose up against Israel and provoked David to take a census of Israel.

**2** David ordered Joab and the military commanders, "Go and count everyone in Israel, from Beersheba to Dan. Then report back to me so I can know the total."

**3** Joab replied, "May the LORD multiply his people a hundred times over! My lord the king, aren't they all your servants already? Why would you want to do this? Why bring guilt on Israel?"

**4** But the king overruled Joab. So Joab left and traveled throughout Israel, then returned to Jerusalem.

**5** Joab reported the census results to David: Israel had 1,100,000 fighting men, and Judah had 470,000.

**6** Joab did not count the tribes of Levi and Benjamin, because the king's order was repulsive to him.

**7** God was displeased with this census, and he struck Israel.

**8** David said to God, "I have sinned terribly by doing this. Please take away your servant's guilt. I have been an utter fool."

**9** The LORD spoke to Gad, David's seer:

**10** "Go and tell David, 'This is what the LORD says: I am giving you three options. Choose one, and I will carry it out against you.'"

**11** Gad went to David and said, "This is what the LORD says — take your choice:

**12** three years of famine, three months of being swept away by your enemies as their swords cut you down, or three days of plague across the land, with the angel of the LORD bringing destruction throughout Israel.' Tell me what answer to take back to the one who sent me."

**13** David answered Gad, "I am in agonizing distress. Let me fall into the LORD's hands, because his mercy is immense. But don't let me fall into human hands."

**14** So the LORD sent a plague on Israel, and seventy thousand Israelites died.

**15** God sent an angel to destroy Jerusalem. But as the angel was carrying out the destruction, the LORD looked down, and his heart was moved with grief over the devastation. He said to the destroying angel, "Stop! That is enough! Pull back!" The angel of the LORD was standing at the threshing floor of Ornan the Jebusite.

**16** David looked up and saw the angel of the LORD suspended between earth and sky, sword drawn, arm extended over Jerusalem. David and the elders, wearing sackcloth, fell facedown on the ground.

**17** David cried out to God, "I am the one who ordered the census! I am the one who sinned! I am the one who did this evil! But these people — they are like sheep. What have they done wrong? O LORD my God, punish me and my family, but stop the plague against your people!"

**18** The angel of the LORD told Gad to instruct David to go up and build an altar to the LORD at Ornan's threshing floor.

**19** David went up, obeying the word Gad had spoken in the LORD's name.

**20** Ornan was threshing wheat when he turned and saw the angel. His four sons who were with him ran and hid.

**21** As David approached, Ornan looked up and saw him. He came out of the threshing floor and bowed before David with his face to the ground.

**22** David said to Ornan, "Sell me this threshing floor site so I can build an altar to the LORD here. Sell it to me at full price, so the plague will be stopped."

**23** Ornan said to David, "Take it! Let my lord the king do whatever he thinks best. Look — I'll donate the oxen for burnt offerings, the threshing sledges for firewood, and the wheat for grain offerings. I give it all freely."

**24** But King David replied, "No — I insist on paying full price. I will not take what belongs to you and give it to the LORD. I will not offer a sacrifice that costs me nothing."

**25** So David paid Ornan six hundred shekels of gold for the site.

**26** David built an altar to the LORD there and offered burnt offerings and fellowship offerings. He called on the LORD, and the LORD answered him by sending fire from heaven onto the altar.

**27** Then the LORD spoke to the angel, who put his sword back in its sheath.

**28** When David saw that the LORD had answered him at Ornan's threshing floor, he continued to sacrifice there.

**29** At that time, the tabernacle of the LORD — the one Moses had made in the wilderness — and the altar of burnt offering were at the high place in Gibeon.

**30** But David could not go there to seek God, because the angel's drawn sword had filled him with terror.

---
## PNEUMA's Meaning Notes

**Verse 1 — Who incited David?** In 2 Samuel 24:1, it is "the anger of the LORD" that incites David to take the census. Here, it is "Satan." This is one of the most important theological shifts in the Hebrew Bible. Between the writing of Samuel and Chronicles, Israel developed a more nuanced understanding of how evil and divine sovereignty relate. The Chronicler cannot attribute incitement to evil directly to God — so an adversary figure absorbs the role. This is not a contradiction but a theological evolution, happening within Scripture itself.

**Verse 13 — David's terrible wisdom:** Faced with three punishments, David chooses the one administered directly by God rather than by human enemies. His reasoning is stunning: God is merciful; humans are not. Even in judgment, David trusts God's character more than human nature. This is the deepest theology in the chapter.

**Verse 15 — "Enough!":** God watches the angel destroy and then says *rav* — "enough." The image is extraordinary: God halting his own judgment mid-course, overcome by compassion. The Hebrew word *vayyinnachem* (he relented/grieved) suggests not simply a change of plan but an emotional response — God is moved.

**Verse 24 — "I will not offer a sacrifice that costs me nothing":** One of the most quoted lines in the Old Testament. David insists on paying full price for the threshing floor. Sacrifice, by definition, must cost something. This principle — that worship cannot be costless — reverberates through the entire biblical tradition.

**Verse 26 — Fire from heaven:** This is the Chronicler's way of marking this spot as sacred ground. Fire from heaven is the sign of divine acceptance: it fell on Elijah's altar (1 Kings 18) and will fall again at Solomon's temple dedication (2 Chronicles 7:1). The threshing floor of Ornan is being identified as the future temple site.

*— PNEUMA*
